title: Recurring unresolved limitation 'sample-representativeness' across 3 independent papers
explanation: 3 independent papers (2021–2026) report an own-work limitation normalized to 'sample-representativeness'. Mixed-fidelity: 3 full-text, 0 abstract-only; score corrected for the ~11x full-text detection bias = 0.642 vs uncorrected 0.642. Methodological diversity: 6 distinct methods (NOTE: diversity/time-span weighting extends beyond opportunity-criteria.md). Resolution is ASSUMED absent — no limitation-resolution relation exists in Phase 3, so 'unresolved' is unverified. evidence_trail.text: Diverse patients’ attitudes towards Artificial Intelligence (AI) in diagnosis
An accuracy self-nudge to reduce misinformation sharing online.
The RCT patient sample consists of predominantly elderly and white participants and is not representative of broader populations.
The qualitative interview pre-study relied on a small convenience sample of 24 patients in one city, preventing strong independent conclusions.
The sample was recruited online and was heavily Democrat-leaning (72.4% when forced to choose), so results may not generalize to samples with different political leanings.

consumer.headline: 3 separate teams ran into the same wall: sample representativeness
consumer.kind_short: A problem that several independent teams ran into
consumer.kind_long: Papers describe the limits of their own work. When separate teams — who did not build on each other — keep reporting the same limit, that is a sign of a real obstacle rather than one group's bad luck.
consumer.strength_meaning: There is real evidence behind this, but it rests on a small number of papers — read them before trusting it.
consumer.why: 3 separate research teams each reported hitting this in their own work. They did not build on each other, so this is unlikely to be one group's bad luck. Their papers span 1 year. We could read 3 of them in full, which is where teams describe what actually went wrong.

caveats.label: Only counted within these 45 papers
caveats.text: These teams all hit this problem within this library of 45 papers, not the whole field. Work outside it may already have solved it. Check before you invest.

caveats.label: Broadly worded
caveats.text: The problem these papers describe is worded broadly enough that they may not be running into quite the same thing.
